question: The original book of yoga was written by  __________. (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Kanada
Patanjali
Bhadra Narayanan
Kapil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Patanjali

Explanation:
The original book of yoga is Yoga Sutra, written by Patanjali. This text is the foundational work of yoga philosophy and contains 195 sutras. Patanjali, also known as Maharshi, was a grammarian and physician. The Yoga Sutra describes the eight limbs of yoga (yama, niyama, asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, samadhi). Other options: Kanada wrote the Vaisheshika philosophy, Bhadra Narayanan wrote a commentary on Yoga Vasistha, and Kapil wrote the Samkhya philosophy. Hence, the correct answer is Patanjali.

☛ How many sutras are in Patanjali's Yoga Sutra? → 195
☛ Other texts written by Patanjali? → Mahabhashya (grammar) and commentary on Charaka Samhita
☛ How many limbs are in Ashtanga Yoga? → 8
☛ Which school of philosophy is associated with Patanjali? → Yoga philosophy
question_hi: योग का मूल ग्रंथ __________ द्वारा लिखा गया था। (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: कणाद
पतंजलि
भद्र नारायण
कपिल
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पतंजलि

Explanation:
योग का मूल ग्रंथ पतंजलि द्वारा रचित योग सूत्र है। यह ग्रंथ योग दर्शन का आधार माना जाता है और इसमें योग के 195 सूत्रों का संकलन है। पतंजलि को महर्षि भी कहा जाता है तथा वे भाष्यकार और चिकित्सा शास्त्र के भी विशेषज्ञ थे। योग सूत्र में अष्टांग योग (यम, नियम, आसन, प्राणायाम, प्रत्याहार, धारणा, ध्यान, समाधि) का वर्णन है। अन्य विकल्प: कणाद ने वैशेषिक दर्शन लिखा, भद्र नारायण ने योग वसिष्ठ पर टीका लिखी, और कपिल ने सांख्य दर्शन लिखा। इस प्रकार सही उत्तर पतंजलि है।

question: Which of these cultures of Buddhism is known for its tantric rituals? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Theravada
Mahayana
Hinayana
None of these
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is None of these

Explanation:
In Buddhism, Tantric rituals are primarily associated with the Vajrayana tradition, which is a sub-school of Mahayana Buddhism. Vajrayana emerged in India around 7th-8th century CE and emphasizes tantras, mantras, yoga, and visualization of deities. Theravada and Hinayana (often considered synonymous with Theravada today) are based on the Pali Tipitaka and do not incorporate tantric practices. While Mahayana includes some esoteric elements, the purely tantric tradition is Vajrayana, which is not listed among the options. Therefore, none of the given cultures is known for tantric rituals.

☛ Origin place of Vajrayana → India
☛ Countries where Vajrayana spread → Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan
☛ Principal text of Theravada → Pali Tipitaka
☛ Form of tantra in Mahayana → Mantrayana
question_hi: बौद्ध धर्म की इनमें से कौन सी संस्कृति तंत्रीय अनुष्ठानों के लिए जानी जाती है? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following Vedas is related to Vedic sacrifices and rituals? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Samveda
Rig Veda
Atharva Veda
Yajurveda
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Yajurveda

Explanation:
Yajurveda is related to Vedic sacrifices and rituals. It contains hymns and procedures to be recited during sacrifices. The word 'Yajuh' means sacrifice or offering. Yajurveda is mainly divided into two parts: Krishna Yajurveda (Black) and Shukla Yajurveda (White). It describes the methods of performing sacrifices, chanting of mantras, and rules for rituals. Among the other Vedas, Rigveda is a collection of hymns, Samaveda is related to music, and Atharvaveda deals with magic and medicine. The primary purpose of Yajurveda is to ensure the successful completion of sacrifices.

ऋग्वेद
अथर्ववेद

Explanation:
यजुर्वेद वैदिक यज्ञों और अनुष्ठानों से संबंधित है। इसमें यज्ञों के दौरान पढ़े जाने वाले मंत्र और प्रक्रियाओं का विस्तृत वर्णन है। 'यजुः' का अर्थ यज्ञ या बलिदान है। यजुर्वेद को मुख्यतः दो भागों में बांटा गया है: कृष्ण यजुर्वेद (काला) और शुक्ल यजुर्वेद (सफेद)। इसमें यज्ञों की विधियां, मंत्रों के उच्चारण और अनुष्ठानों के नियम दिए गए हैं। अन्य वेदों में, ऋग्वेद स्तुतियों का संग्रह है, सामवेद संगीत से संबंधित है, और अथर्ववेद जादू-टोने और आयुर्वेद से जुड़ा है। यजुर्वेद का प्रमुख उद्देश्य यज्ञों को सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न कराना है।

question: Which is the branch of Buddhism called the 'Great' vehicle? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Theravada
Thunderbolt
Mahayana
Abhidhamma Pitta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahayana

Explanation:
Mahayana is the branch of Buddhism called the 'Great Vehicle' (Maha meaning great, Yana meaning vehicle). It is one of the two major branches of Buddhism, the other being Theravada. Mahayana emerged around the 1st century BCE. This tradition emphasizes the ideal of the Bodhisattva, who seeks Buddhahood for the benefit of all beings. Its scriptures include Sutras written in Sanskrit. Mahayana worships not only the Buddha but also numerous Bodhisattvas. It is predominantly practiced in China, Japan, Korea, and Tibet.

question: Who was the founder of the Harik dynasty? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Infant
Udayan
Bimbisara
Dhananand
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bimbisara

Explanation:
The Haryanka dynasty was an ancient ruling dynasty of Magadha. It was founded by Bimbisara around 544 BCE. Bimbisara was one of the most powerful rulers of Magadha, who expanded the kingdom through matrimonial alliances and conquests. He allied with kingdoms like Kosala, Vaishali, and Madra, and annexed Anga into Magadha. Bimbisara was also known as Shrenika and was a follower of Buddhism. After him, his son Ajatashatru succeeded the throne. The Haryanka dynasty transformed Magadha into a major political power, laying the foundation for the later Maurya Empire.

question: Which of the following was a dockyard in the Harappan site?  (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Dholavira
Lothal
Kalibanga
Banvali
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lothal.

Explanation:
Lothal, located in Gujarat, is a prominent Harappan site known for its dockyard. A rectangular brick-built dock was discovered here, indicating maritime trade. Evidence of beads, seals, and foreign artifacts suggests trade with Mesopotamia and Egypt. Dholavira is famous for its water management system, Kalibanga for ploughed fields, and Banvali in Rajasthan lacks a dockyard. Lothal's dockyard, measuring 214 m by 36 m, was used for ship berthing and cargo handling, making it a vital center for Harappan sea trade.

Explanation:
Stupa is a Buddhist architectural structure, typically a hemispherical mound containing relics of Buddha or important monks. It is used for prayer and meditation, not as a residence or open house. The most famous stupa is the Sanchi Stupa, built by Emperor Ashoka. Option 1 'Salinity mound' refers to a specific geographical formation, but it is not directly related to a stupa. 'Salinity mound' means a mound of salt, which is not synonymous with a stupa. Hence this option is incorrect. While a stupa can be considered a prayer hall, that is its function, not its definition. The correct answer is 'Salinity mound', but since the question asks what a stupa is, the correct answer should actually be a prayer hall or relic mound. However, given the options, 'Salinity mound' is marked as correct, which is misleading. Nevertheless, based on the provided correct answer, we note that a stupa is not a saline mound.

स्तूप एक बौद्ध स्थापत्य संरचना है, जो आमतौर पर अर्धगोलाकार टीले के रूप में होती है और इसमें बुद्ध या अन्य महत्वपूर्ण भिक्षुओं के अवशेष रखे जाते हैं। यह प्रार्थना और ध्यान के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है, न कि आवास या खुले घर के रूप में। सबसे प्रसिद्ध स्तूप साँची का स्तूप है, जिसे सम्राट अशोक ने बनवाया था। विकल्प 1 में 'लवणता टीला' का अर्थ किसी विशेष भौगोलिक संरचना से है, लेकिन स्तूप से इसका सीधा संबंध नहीं। 'लवणता टीला' का अर्थ नमक के टीले से है, जो स्तूप का पर्याय नहीं है। इसलिए यह विकल्प गलत है। स्तूप को प्रार्थना कक्ष के रूप में भी जाना जाता है, लेकिन यह उसका मुख्य कार्य है। सही उत्तर 'लवणता टीला' है, जो गलत है, क्योंकि स्तूप कोई लवणता टीला नहीं है। बल्कि स्तूप एक धार्मिक स्मारक है।

question: Which of the following is considered to be the last of 24 Jain Tirthankaras?  (RPF Constable 2018 (22/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Rishab
Ajitnath
Parsvnath
Mahavira
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahavira

Explanation:
In Jainism, there is a tradition of 24 Tirthankaras, and the last (24th) Tirthankara is Mahavira Swami. He was born in 599 BCE at Kundagrama near Vaishali. Among the options, Rishabha is the first Tirthankara, Ajitnath is the second, and Parsvanath is the 23rd. Mahavira revived Jain principles and preached the five great vows: non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness. He renounced his home at the age of 30, practiced severe penance for 12 years, and attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience). He is also known as Vardhamana, Jina, and Nirgrantha.

question: Who was the successor of Chandragupta Maurya? (RPF Constable 2018 (22/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: The 'lion-colored pillar-head' in Sarnath was built by whom? (RPF Constable 2018 (22/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: From which country is the famous traveler Fahyan associated? (RPF Constable 2018 (22/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Italy
Persia
Greece
China
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is China

Explanation:
Faxian (Fahyan) was a famous Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler who visited India between 399 CE and 414 CE. His main objective was to obtain Buddhist scriptures and visit sacred Buddhist sites. He traveled during the Gupta period and recorded his experiences in a book titled 'Fo-guo-ji' (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms). This work provides valuable details about the social, economic, and religious conditions of India at that time. Faxian's accounts help historians understand the glory of the Gupta Empire. He visited important places like Taxila, Nalanda, and Pataliputra. His journey is a significant source of cultural exchange between China and India.

question_hi: प्रसिद्ध यात्री फाह्यान किस देश से संबंधित थे? (RPF Constable 2018 (22/01/2019) Shift 3)

question: In which of the following places was the Buddha received knowledge? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 1)

Sarnath

solution:

question: During whose reign Chinese traveler Fa-Hienya, who visited India? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:
The Chinese Buddhist monk Fa-hien visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (also known as Vikramaditya) of the Gupta Empire, between 399-414 CE. He came in search of Buddhist scriptures and traveled extensively across the Indian subcontinent, visiting places like Pataliputra, Kannauj, Mathura, and Takshashila. His travelogue, 'Fo-kuo-ki' (Account of Buddhist Kingdoms), provides valuable insights into the Gupta period's society, economy, religion, and administration. Fa-hien mentioned the coexistence of Hinduism and Buddhism, efficient governance, and social welfare activities. He also noted the absence of severe punishments and the prevalence of vegetarianism among the people. His account is a crucial primary source for understanding ancient Indian history.

question: Who wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Harsha
Ashoka
Pulakeshin II
Chandragupta Maurya
solution:

Explanation:
The three Sanskrit plays Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda were written by Emperor Harshavardhana (606-647 AD). Harsha was not only a great ruler but also a renowned literary figure. He personally composed these plays. Ratnavali is a love story, Priyadarshika deals with the romance between Princess Priyadarshika and King Udayana, and Nagananda is a play influenced by Buddhism. Harsha's court included scholars like Banabhatta, who wrote Harshacharita. Harsha made Kannauj his capital and organized the Kumbh Mela at Prayag.

question_hi: रत्नावली, प्रियदर्शिका और नागानंद के रचियता कौन थे? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 2)

question: Who among the following was called as the "Indian Napoleon"? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 1)
options: Skandagupta
Chandragupta II
Samudragupta
Pulakeshin II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Samudragupta

Explanation:
Samudragupta (335-380 CE) was called the 'Indian Napoleon'. He was the greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty, and his reign is considered the golden age of the Gupta Empire. He conducted extensive military campaigns, conquering most of the kingdoms in northern India, and also sent expeditions to southern India. His victories are described in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad pillar inscription), composed by his court poet Harishena. Samudragupta was also a patron of music and arts; his coins depict him playing the veena, which is evidence of his cultural interests.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसे "भारतीय नेपोलियन" कहा जाता था? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 1)

question: The term 'Bodhisattva' is related to which religion? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:
